speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In Singapore's relatively short history as a nation, the National Day Parade has always taken centre-stage as we celebrate each year of independence.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Members in this House have attended these National Day Parades.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And many of you have kindly told me after each parade that it was well done, the mood was lifted, there was a sense of togetherness as Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, I think, in turn, the National Day Parade has served our nation well – both as a rallying call for all Singaporeans to stay united but also a clear statement of our confidence and determination to succeed collectively, no matter the odds.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Through thick and thin, good times or bad, it showed Singaporeans celebrating and standing firm as one people, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am so used to the mask that I spoke with it; forgot to take it off!

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is what COVID-19 has done to us.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Not all countries celebrate their national days the way that we have or put the national day parade as centre-stage.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There is a history to the National Day Parade.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But that inaugural NDP would set the example for the subsequent 54 years.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That first NDP was held at the Padang with 21-gun salute as the President reviewed various contingents that we have become accustomed to the SAF, the Police, NTUC, uniformed youth organisations and so forth.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The military units then marched from the Padang into Chinatown, to waving crowds.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Fireworks at that time, took place at the Padang and Fort Canning.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It followed the Parade and it adorned the skies.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: At night, there was an illuminated sea dragon, 150 metres long, 12 metres tall, lit up by 12,500 bulbs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It may be prosaic to us today, but at that time, it was quite spectacular.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It sailed across what is today's Marina Bay.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: By all accounts, it was an extraordinary event, especially for a nation that was barely a year old.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Could the money have been put to better use?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Remember that our fledgling nation had a host of unsolved problems – high unemployment, few could afford to own homes, high drop-out rates even at Primary 6, inadequate medical care.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Why did the first NDP proceed that way?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Because the unity and collective confidence for the future that it engendered among Singaporeans was priceless.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It showed to the rest of the world that despite great difficulties, ours was a country that would not be beaten down, ours was a people that will rise and overcome.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Without that unity and confidence, Singapore could not have survived, let alone thrived against the challenges that our founding generation faced.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Member of this House will readily recognise that subsequent National Day Parades take reference from and pay homage to that seminal NDP of 1966 – both in spirit and form.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: At each National Day, as we did during the first, we are making a conscious act of the will.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is a willful event that we have said we will celebrate, whether individually or as one people, to celebrate each National Day with the same indomitable spirit, never mind the prevailing difficulties and never mind the differences among people.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As Singapore prospered over the years, that focus on survival, overcoming difficulties, even unity, may have inadvertently diminished.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, over the years, the NDP has now evolved into softer tones.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It has become more individualistic, more of an affirmation of what Singapore is and what being Singaporean means to each citizen.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, you would remember the videos that we played in previous NDPs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They had resonance, Singaporeans liked them because they focused on individuals, differences among our people and yet the unity that we could form from it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That may be today's zeitgeist but we should never forget that the first NDP and the origin of that spirit remains essential for our nationhood.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When the NDP Executive Committee (Exco) revealed some details for NDP 2020, some Singaporeans felt that these celebrations were wasteful and that the same resources ought to be spent elsewhere, especially in light of the impact that COVID-19 had on our economy and jobs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have had four Budgets, and each time, we dig into our reserves, to make sure that we protect lives and protect livelihoods and jobs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I appreciate that point of view and agree fully with them that we ought to be prudent.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But we should guard against the mood of despondency overcoming us or allow individual preferences to divide us.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If we allow despair to prevail in our national psyche, particularly in this COVID-19 pandemic, then, I say that would be the greatest harm to the future of Singapore – much more devastating than the economic impact, the loss of jobs and businesses.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Even through those difficult years, Singaporeans chose to celebrate the National Day Parade as we have always done, and rallied together.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In fact, experts have to go very far back to find events that matched the equivalent magnitude of the impact.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Events like World War I, the Great Depression of the 1920s and 1930s, World War II are cited.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For tiny Singapore alone, the infections will last many more months.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the impact of disrupted lives and livelihoods will last even longer.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If at this early stage, Singaporeans lose their mettle, their inner strength and equanimity, lose their resolve, weaken their resilience, sharpen their differences, then, we are already in trouble.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This is not the Singapore that you and I know.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This is not the Singapore spirit that has ensured our survival through many previous hardships.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, I say, despite the difficulties and indeed, because of the more challenging times that are ahead, we should celebrate this year's NDP as we have done before and just as our founding generation did during the first NDP.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That, for us, is the most important aspect for this year's NDP.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Exco for NDP 2020 has stayed true to its roots, but has adapted the format to reduce the risk of infection in the face of an imminent threat from COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Their concept, which Ms Denise Phua asked about, is a simple one.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Not being able to hold the NDP at a central location with large crowds should not prevent Singaporeans from expressing their pride and love for Singapore and the call for unity.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We may be physically apart, but we want to join in spirit as one people with that same confidence and optimism and unity that the founding generation fostered despite harsher and grim circumstances.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Most elements will follow the traditions of past NDPs, but some items will be new.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The morning segment will begin with the Prime Minister's National Day message.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The President will be the Reviewing Officer but for a much smaller scale parade comprising only SAF and Home Team contingents.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: SAF helicopters carrying the Singapore flag will fly over the Padang and also make their way across the housing estates through Singapore.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When the Anthem is played at the Padang, flag-raising ceremonies around the island will take place concurrently, so that Singaporeans across the island, whether in their constituencies, camps, workplaces or elsewhere will be singing Majulah Singapura in unison.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In past NDPs that Members of this House have enjoyed, the SAF aircraft could fly only over the NDP site, whether at the Padang or the Float.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: With Changi Airport being one of the busiest in the world, that was all the air space and the air time that we could be allocated for NDP.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We expect air travel to pick up in the months ahead and I know that MOT and CAAS are working very hard.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But this year, let us turn this into an opportunity so that the SAF aircraft can fly in formation over the heartlands of Singapore, so that Singaporeans can watch it from their homes.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Mobile columns from the SAF and Home Team will also travel through various parts of the island.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: With them will be the frontline heroes and heroines who have shown exemplary sacrifice and courage in fighting this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I know that Singaporeans want to thank them personally.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The NDP will be a good occasion from a safe distance for Singaporeans to cheer them on and show them their much deserved appreciation.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Instead of an NDP show with thousands of participants, there will be a boutique studio show at night, with performances by some local artistes and talents which will be broadcasted live.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There will be interactive elements for Singaporeans to sing along, join in the Pledge during the show.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And as we do each year, there will be fireworks across a few sites in Singapore to cap the day's and night's events over the Singapore skyline, both in the Central Business District and the HDB heartlands.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The fireworks will not be as long or spectacular as recent centralised NDPs, but I hope that it will lift the spirits of Singaporeans all across the island.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: To facilitate Singaporeans joining in as one people and one nation, the NDP Exco provides what they call a "Singapore Together Pack".

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Mr Leon Perera and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about this.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Exco had engaged various groups in designing this pack and has also taken in public feedback.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Full details are still being worked out but let me share what I can.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Singaporeans will find the bag for the pack useful as a reusable grocery bag; it is practical, foldable into a small pouch.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The designs on the bag are by local artists with disabilities and some of our Primary 5 pupils – each design an expression of their feelings for their country and fellow citizens, and their hopes for the future.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As families will be at home, there is no need for single-use water bottles, neither plastic clappers nor packaging.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: These have been done away with, to reduce waste.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There will be items that express our collective love and wishes for Singapore like the National flag – a full-sized cloth flag, a handheld one – as well as iron-on patches for your masks, a pledge card and face tattoos.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Well-wishing corporations have asked to add to the pack items to express their gratitude for what Singapore has given them, by giving back to Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Companies are also offering vouchers and we have decided to put them as an e-discount booklet.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For every NDP, the Exco aims to be inclusive and they take in views and accommodate different interests where possible.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But let me just say this as a gentle caution.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If every interest group pushes for its own agenda especially during the NDP, then our common ground to celebrate this national event shrinks.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Because the Exco simply will never be able to satisfy every request adequately.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For this generation, our response will determine whether Singapore continues to thrive in the post-COVID world.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As with every crisis, people have a choice to make – to overcome or be overwhelmed.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As we did at the very first NDP, I urge all Members of this House and all Singaporeans to reaffirm our unity, to reaffirm our resilience, bonded by the same vision and optimism that Singapore will prevail and overcome the challenges that this COVID-19 pandemic has brought upon us.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The months ahead will be trying and the difficulties ahead will test our resolve and cohesion.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Despite all of this, Singaporeans can, and Singapore will, celebrate NDP 2020 with confidence and hope for a brighter future.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The Minister mentioned that the total number of packs is for 80% of the households.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: What was the redemption percentage for SG50 packs?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Is 80% sufficient to cater to the anticipated demand?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We will leave them as they wish and so we will produce 80% which should be adequate.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The difficulty that the NDP Exco had is trying to shoot a moving target.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, when they presented to me the plans, they had a number of scenarios.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: One scenario was – this was before circuit breaker – the normal NDP, the usual, thousands upon thousands.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: An interim scenario is where you can have crowds of 50 or even 500.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When I saw the plans, I said "Let us dispense with Options A and B.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Let us just assume the worst that COVID-19 will bring".

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: You can come out of the circuit breaker but in August, suppose something happens and we have to reimpose the circuit breaker.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The mood will be down, Singaporeans will become despondent and that is the time when we say, "Come together, have this National Parade even despite your fears, come out and celebrate" – not come out literally, because you must stay at home; but come out in spirit and celebrate.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have had two months off circuit breaker.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Some people actually like it; they find working from home more productive and they found a sweet spot.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For others, there is actually fear, fear to come out, fear to join others.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, when I read notes that say why do we not be prudent, I completely agree with them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But I want to make sure that this is not despondency or fear.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Because for many heartlanders, these are physical touch points, commonalities, that when they wave the flag, it is the same flag, when they have tattoos, it is a physical token for them to latch on to.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Never dismiss these symbols even though the cost is little.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you hand in your request and you know there are groups that will want it, whether it is various groups, please let MINDEF know and we will try to facilitate for more.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am sure we can all agree that it is important for the country to rally together to have a keynote that underlines our unity during this difficult time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister has explained the plan with the funpack.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But my question is, really, for something like a funpack to serve the purpose that it is intended for, consultation and buy-in from the public may be useful to understand whether most people would really want to have this and whether it would serve that purpose of banishing the despondency, raising the spirits, rallying and unifying everyone.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, learning from this experience, I wonder whether there could be a bigger role for consultation in future before a very large or elaborate logistical exercise, such as distributing packs for everyone, is undertaken.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is, I understand that REACH set up an online poll to solicit views of Singaporeans about the funpack.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I was wondering how long this poll was up for and what the results of this poll showed, if that is available.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I agree fully with him that we need to engage groups to see what for them represents a good way to celebrate our National Day Parade.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But as I said in my primary answer, while the Exco needs to be open, forward-leaning, consultative, there is a balance.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If every group with their individual preferences decide to use the National Day Parade to press for their differences, then I think the Exco has a very difficult task.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Because it will never be able to satisfy all groups, it will never be able to be all things to all men.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It will have to balance, as we do every year.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In previous years, when they, even ourselves, who are conscious about climate change, want to reduce and they press for disposable water bottles, the Exco had to balance the need for elderly and children who need bottled water.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The disposable water bottles are actually recyclable the Exco even looked at giving reusable water bottles, then putting water stands, whether it is at the Floating platform or the stadium or Padang, but they found it was undoable.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, they did the next best thing; instead of two small bottles, they gave one big bottle, which will reduce the amount of plastic, I presume.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is always these choices to make between different interests.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the more important point is this: for this balance to be struck, how does each individual group want to press for its own interests?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have gone past race, religion and language, I hope – I am talking about the NDP show.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am still very careful that there must be proper representation, that even when we carry soft stories that we should represent all of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But if any interest group decides to say, "My interests are not shown.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If Mr Perera wants to know that, he can put it to that Ministry and I am sure that Ministry will give him a full reply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, there is already a reduction but that is based, as Minister said, on estimations and based on past experience.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would it not be better to just ask Singaporeans whether they want to opt out of receiving the funpack, so that we can get a more accurate figure that will reduce the wastage?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second clarification is what Member Cheng Li Hui asked previously, what will we be doing with the excess funpacks that are not collected?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, let me record my appreciation of thanks to the NDP Exco 2020.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I worked with them for the last six months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As what NCMP Leon Perera has asked, we actually have been on the ground for the last six months getting feedback from the green groups and working together with them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, this morning, we had another Zoom call with them to explain why we had a funpack, why we had certain items in there, and it was a very positive conversation that we had.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I want to thank the NDP Exco for the forward-thinking, for really listening.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been a privilege working with the Chairman, Brigadier-General Frederick Choo.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, I would suggest that the Minister make him NDP Exco Chairman in 2021 since he did not get to organise a full NDP this year, and he really has done an amazing job trying to find the middle ground and making very difficult decisions.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I had known that he had been involved and helped us for the last six months.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But I chose not to cite his help in the reply to Mr Leon Perera because, it is better that Mr Ng himself said it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Otherwise, they will say, you know, whatever they will say.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I am not sure if he would want it, but nonetheless, we will think about it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Why not have, before each NDP, a full public consultation as I think was the point that Mr Perera made.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Just for practical purposes – Members of this House lead organisations, you are in businesses or in your organisations, you should know – there is a limit beyond which analysis becomes paralysis.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: You want to have feedback but you have to ultimately make a decision.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I cite this but I am not suggesting you make this an issue, but in terms of carbon production, my fighter planes probably produce more.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: While we "rah rah" to the zoom of fighter aircraft, jet fuel is being burnt up there.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, I think there is a limit to consultation.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We will be forward-leaning, we will take in views, but there is a balance to be struck.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There is a time for every activity, a season for everything under the heavens.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have been divided like never before by a little organism, barely 0.125 microns.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Relatives have been separated, grandparents from their grandchildren, couples, even spouses.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For the healthcare workers, some were so fearful.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They were not fearful about going to work but they were so fearful that they would pass on their infections if they got infected to their families, that they chose to stay away from their families, and the hospitals facilitated and found hotel rooms for them to stay alone.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Never a time have we been so physically divided.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Never a time have we been so psychologically affected.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I say this to you not to frighten you, but the months ahead will be harder.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This is not a time to show up our divisions.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It does not mean we do not ask for feedback.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But this is maybe a time, in gentle tones, to put aside some of our differences and come together.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Louis Ng, you have some more clarifications?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Sorry, Sir, there really is just a remaining concern which is what will we do with the excess packs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think I understand we might be donating them or giving them to some other groups.
